intro: Asking for a change formally, using the polite conditional and checking the details before agreeing.
p.reserva.consejo: It is feminine: «la reserva». You say «hacer», «cambiar» or «cancelar una reserva».
p.habitación.consejo: It is feminine and the stress falls on the last syllable: a-bi-ta-THYON.
p.fecha.consejo: It is feminine: «la fecha». You say «cambiar la fecha» and «la fecha de llegada».
p.cambiar.consejo: With things you say «cambiar la fecha»; with places, «cambiar de habitación».
p.comprobar.consejo: It changes o → ue: «compruebo», «compruebas». Before agreeing, check the details.
p.disponible.consejo: It works for rooms, tables and people. It is the same in masculine and feminine.
p.conservar.consejo: Here «se conserva» means «it stays the same». The v sounds like a b.
p.suplemento.consejo: It is masculine: «el suplemento». You pay it for something added or for a change.
p.incluido.consejo: It agrees: «incluido», «incluida». A typical question: «¿está incluido el desayuno?».
p.desayuno.consejo: It is masculine: «el desayuno». The verb is «desayunar»: «desayuno a las ocho».
p.podría.consejo: It is the conditional of «poder». It makes the request more formal than «puedes».
p.sería posible.consejo: It is used with an infinitive: «¿sería posible cambiar la fecha?». It is very formal.
p.a nombre de.consejo: It is used for bookings and orders: «la reserva está a nombre de Ruiz».
b1.titulo: A formal request has two parts
b1.texto:
To ask for something formally, use **¿Podría…?** or **¿Sería posible…?**. Then give the reason or say what you prefer: **¿Podría cambiar la fecha? Me gustaría conservar la misma habitación.**

The other person may offer an option, explain a limit or ask a question. Before agreeing, **check the details**: dates, price and what is included.

In a service or with a stranger, use **usted**: *¿podría decirme…?*, *déjeme comprobarlo*, *espere un momento*. The same pattern works for appointments, restaurant bookings and paperwork.
b2.f0.texto: Good morning, could you help me with a booking?
b2.f1.texto: Of course, what name is it under?
b2.f3.texto: Perfect, I can see it now.
b2.f4.texto: Would it be possible to arrive on Saturday instead of Friday?
b2.f5.texto: One moment, I am going to check.
b2.f6.texto: The same room is available with a surcharge of twenty euros.
b2.f7.texto: Could you tell me whether breakfast is included?
b2.f9.texto: All right, thank you very much.
b4.texto:
The conditional (**-ía**) makes the request more formal:

- **¿Podría** + infinitive? *¿Podría decirme la hora?*
- **¿Sería posible** + infinitive? *¿Sería posible cambiar la fecha?*
- **Me gustaría** + infinitive: *Me gustaría conservar la habitación.*
- **Quería** + infinitive (imperfect of politeness): *Quería cambiar la reserva.*

With **usted**, the command uses the subjunctive form: **déjeme**, **dígame**, **espere**. With **tú**: **déjame**, **dime**, **espera**.
b4.e1.texto: Would it be possible to change the booking date?
b4.e2.texto: I wanted to book a double room.
b5.f0.texto: The hotel lobby smells of polished wood and fresh flowers.
b5.f1.texto: A ceiling fan turns slowly above the leather armchairs.
b5.f2.texto: Behind the counter, a golden clock shows nine o'clock sharp.
b5.f3.texto: The keys hang from small hooks like fruits made of metal.
b5.f4.texto: Through the revolving door comes a cold air smelling of rain.
b5.f5.texto: Elena leaves her suitcase next to the counter and breathes deeply.
b5.f6.texto: The receptionist looks up from the screen and smiles kindly.
b5.f7.texto: His fingers run over the keyboard with a light tapping.
b5.f8.texto: On the map on the wall, a green light marks the free room.
b5.f9.texto: Outside, the raindrops draw long paths on the glass.
b6.o0: Llegar el sábado, no el viernes.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! She only wants to change the arrival date.
b6.o1.refuerzo: No: the room is the same. The date changes.
b6.o2.refuerzo: On the contrary: she asks whether breakfast is still included.
b6.pregunta: What change does Elena ask for?
b7.frase: ¿____ decirme si el desayuno está incluido?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! The conditional «podría» is the politest form.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Puedo» is «I can»: you are asking about the other person. Here you need «podría».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Pude» is a past tense. It does not work to ask for something now.
b7.pregunta: Which form makes the request more formal?
b8.frase: ¿Sería posible cambiar la fecha de la reserva?
b8.traduccion: Would it be possible to change the booking date?
b9.o0.refuerzo: There is a cost: the room is the same, but with a surcharge.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! That is the surcharge the receptionist mentions.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Breakfast stays included: it is not paid separately.
b9.pregunta: What extra cost does the change have?
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Could you help me with a booking?»
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Se conserva» means it stays the same.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Conservas» is tú. The subject is «el desayuno»: third person.
b11.o2.refuerzo: A conjugated verb is missing, not an infinitive.
b12.o0.refuerzo: That's it! With «usted», the command takes the form «espere».
b12.o1.refuerzo: It is the «tú» form, more informal. With strangers, «usted».
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is the «vosotros» form, for several friends.
b12.pregunta: The receptionist asks you to wait. What does he say?
p.comprobarlo.consejo: The pronoun «lo» joins the infinitive «comprobar». The stress stays on «BAR»: kom-pro-BAR-lo.
p.decirme.consejo: «¿Podría decirme…?» is a formal question. The «ci» sounds “thi” in Spain: de-THIR-me.
p.conserva.consejo: Third person of «conservar»; «se conserva» means “it stays as it was”. The «v» sounds like a b.
p.vestíbulo.consejo: The accent on the «í» shows the stress, three syllables from the end. The «v» sounds like a b: bes-TI-bu-lo.
p.pulida.consejo: Participle of «pulir», used as an adjective. It agrees with «madera»: «madera pulida».
p.ventilador.consejo: It is masculine: «el ventilador». The «v» sounds like a b, and the stress falls on the last syllable: ben-ti-la-DOR.
p.techo.consejo: It is masculine: «el techo». The «ch» is like in “cheese”. A «ventilador de techo» hangs from the ceiling.
p.butacas.consejo: Plural of «la butaca». It also means a seat in a cinema or theatre. The «c» before a sounds k.
p.cuero.consejo: It is masculine: «el cuero». “Ue” is one syllable: KWE-ro. “Butacas de cuero” are leather armchairs.
p.ganchos.consejo: Plural of «el gancho». The «ch» is like in “cheese”: GAN-chos. Keys and coats hang from them.
p.frutos.consejo: Plural of «el fruto». «Fruta» is the fruit you eat; «fruto» is the botanical fruit or a result.
p.metal.consejo: It is masculine: «el metal». It ends in «-l», so the stress is on the last syllable: me-TAL.
p.giratoria.consejo: Feminine of «giratorio», agreeing with «puerta». The «g» before i sounds like a strong h: hi-ra-TO-rya.
p.recepcionista.consejo: The same word is used for men and women: «el recepcionista», «la recepcionista». The «c» before e or i sounds “th”.
p.vista.consejo: It is feminine: «la vista». “Levantar la vista” is to look up. The «v» sounds like a b: BIS-ta.
p.golpeteo.consejo: From «golpear» (to hit). The ending «-eo» makes it a repeated sound. «E-o» are two separate vowels: gol-pe-TE-o.
p.ligero.consejo: The opposite of «pesado». The «g» before e sounds like a strong h: li-HE-ro. It agrees: «un golpeteo ligero».
p.dibujan.consejo: Third person plural of «dibujar». The «j» sounds like a strong h and the «b» is soft: di-BU-han.
p.caminos.consejo: Plural of «el camino». The raindrops on the glass leave long «caminos». The «c» before a sounds k.
p.espere.consejo: Command for «usted»: «espera» (tú) becomes «espere». It is the polite form used in services.
